# neon-ducklake documentation

> neon-ducklake harvests the NEON Data API into a DuckDB ducklake-extension catalog lake, builds per-site lakes of stacked NEON data with full AVU metadata on the CyVerse Data Store, and records every AVU change in a MESA history. The lakes are public and readable anonymously over HTTPS. It covers the three published datasets (the catalog lake of NEON Data API metadata, the per-site lakes of stacked NEON data, and the MESA AVU history), with their tables, columns, coverage, freshness and tested queries, and how the pipeline builds, publishes, refreshes and tests them. The source repository is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) bundle: every page carries YAML frontmatter with type, provenance (generated/sources), and lifecycle (status/stale_after) fields.

Every page below is listed with three addresses that all return the same content: the rendered HTML page, its Markdown twin (page URL + `index.md`, served as text/markdown with the OKF frontmatter), and the raw source file on GitHub. Fetch whichever your tool is allowed to reach; many sandboxes permit github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com but not *.github.io.

```
Site page        https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/<path>/
Markdown twin    https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/<path>/index.md
Raw source       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/<path>.md      (branch main; a moving target)

Content page     /data/collection/  ->  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/data/collection.md
```

The legacy form https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/<path>.md also still returns the same Markdown, for links made before 2026-09-10.

## Overview

- [neon-ducklake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/): neon-ducklake harvests the NEON Data API into a DuckDB ducklake-extension catalog lake, builds per-site lakes of stacked NEON data with full AVU metadata on the CyVerse Data Store, and records every AVU change in a MESA history. The lakes are public and readable anonymously over HTTPS. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/index.md

## Data

- [The published collection](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/collection/): What is in the public neon-ducklake collection on the CyVerse Data Store (catalog lake, site lakes, raw NEON files, reports, AVU history, the history spool), which code writes each path, and how to read it anonymously over HTTPS. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/collection/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/data/collection.md
- [Catalog lake (neon_catalog.ducklake)](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/): Dataset card for the Phase-1 catalog lake: NEON Data API metadata (202 products, 81 sites, 6 releases, availability, locations, taxonomy) and an inventory of 3,215,813 non-AOP data files, as one DuckDB ducklake-extension lake readable anonymously over HTTPS. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/data/catalog-lake.md
- [Catalog lake: column reference](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake-columns/): Every table and view of the neon-ducklake catalog lake with its one-line description, row count, key and the name and DuckDB type of every column, taken from information_schema and table_catalog on 2026-11-24. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake-columns/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/data/catalog-lake-columns.md
- [Site lakes (neon_<site>.ducklake)](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/): Dataset card for the Phase-2 site lakes: stacked, typed NEON data tables plus file, variable, sensor-position and taxa tables for one NEON site each. Two sites are published (SRER and KONZ), both partial sample runs, readable anonymously over HTTPS. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/data/site-lakes.md
- [AVU history (.mesa/ducklake)](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/): Dataset card for the MESA AVU history of the neon-ducklake project: 104,964 add/delete events on 11,393 Data Store paths in six plain Parquet snapshot files, how they get there (journal, spool, recorder, mesa-ducklake), their columns, and how to read them without the MESA catalog. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/data/avu-history.md

## Engineering

- [Architecture](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/architecture/): neon-ducklake's two phases (the catalog lake from the NEON API, then per-site lakes with full AVUs), the stages of a streamed and a whole-site run, and the local and Data Store layouts. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/architecture/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/engineering/architecture.md
- [How lakes are built and published](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/building-lakes/): Why neon-ducklake builds every lake on local disk and uploads it, how a build ends (one snapshot, CHECKPOINT, DETACH, no .wal), the upload order with checksums and the catalog file last, versioned site-lake catalogs behind CURRENT, and how AVU history reaches .mesa/ducklake through the spool and the recorder. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/building-lakes/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/engineering/building-lakes.md
- [Running the pipeline](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/running/): Requirements, install, secrets and configuration for neon-ducklake; the quick start for the catalog lake and one site; the full sweep; workers on several VMs; and how to rebuild or refresh the lakes after a new NEON release. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/running/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/engineering/running.md
- [Adding a site or product](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/extending/): How neon-ducklake selects sites and products (from the catalog lake, not from a hand-kept list), how to build and publish one more site, what happens when NEON adds a product, and which code to change for products that need special handling or for a new catalog table. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/extending/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/engineering/extending.md
- [Testing and verification](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/testing/): neon-ducklake's hermetic pytest suite (no NEON, iRODS or MESA access; in-memory fakes of python-irodsclient and the other services), ruff lint, and the verify commands that check the catalog lake, a site, and the MESA history and gate eviction. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/testing/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/engineering/testing.md

## Design records

- [Design plan](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/PLAN/): The approved neon-ducklake design: phases, architecture, catalog tables, AVU vocabulary, bulk writer and history, and verification. Later decisions in SCALING, CONTRACTS, STREAMING and RUNBOOK take precedence. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/PLAN/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/PLAN.md
- [Internal contracts](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/CONTRACTS/): The interfaces every neon-ducklake module codes against: shared modules, catalog-lake and site-lake tables and columns, desired AVUs, uploads, and the ontology stores, with their amendment rounds. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/CONTRACTS/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/CONTRACTS.md
- [Streaming and multi-VM execution](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/STREAMING/): The contract of the streaming pipeline and of workers on several VMs: chunks, per-chunk stages and return codes, the versioned site lake on the Data Store, history backends and the recorder, claims, journal backups, and the orchestrator. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/STREAMING/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/STREAMING.md
- [Scaling to 81 sites](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/SCALING/): How the neon-ducklake site pipeline scales to all 81 NEON sites: what varies across sites, hard limits and the decisions they forced, the orchestrator, and measured throughput. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/SCALING/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/SCALING.md
- [Runbook](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/RUNBOOK/): Operating the neon-ducklake site pipeline: prerequisites, the orchestrator, one site or all sites, monitoring, recovery, review, refreshing after a NEON release, eviction, streaming, workers and the recorder. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/RUNBOOK/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/RUNBOOK.md
- [Workers on CyVerse DE VMs](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/DE_SANDBOX/): Running neon-ducklake workers on several CyVerse Discovery Environment VMs: roles, VM setup, secrets without a keyring, the worker, the history recorder, stale claims, curation across VMs, and troubleshooting. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/DE_SANDBOX/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/DE_SANDBOX.md

## About

- [For AI agents](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/about/ai-agents/): How agents should consume the neon-ducklake documentation (llms.txt, per-page Markdown with OKF frontmatter, raw GitHub sources, trust signals) and how to get the data itself: attach the public lakes read-only with DuckDB, or use neon-mcp for the live NEON API. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/about/ai-agents/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/about/ai-agents.md

## Meta

- [Full corpus in one file](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/llms-full.txt): every page's Markdown with frontmatter, links made absolute; about 297 KB, roughly 76,000 tokens. Prefer it over fetching pages one at a time.
- [Documentation update log](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/log/): dated history of changes to this bundle.
- [For AI agents](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/about/ai-agents/): endpoints, trust signals, and what to do if you cannot fetch this site.
- [Sitemap](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/sitemap.xml) and [robots.txt](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/robots.txt): crawlers honour only the origin https://idss-mesa.github.io/robots.txt, which is equally permissive.
- [MESA project site](https://idss-mesa.github.io/llms.txt): origin-level llms.txt indexing the MESA site, this documentation, and the MESA software repositories.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake): the bundle itself; `docs/` mirrors the site paths one to one.

If you want CyVerse data rather than documentation, install the MESA MCP servers (or connect to a hosted endpoint) and call their tools; the agent guide explains how.
